info.title: Highbay MCP Software Factory Control Plane
info.description: The Highbay project server: coding agents propose, build, test and verify changes to a Goa and Goa-AI service through its MCP tools, and the user agrees each change and approves its result on its views page.

get.description: Return the builder's assignment list, as list_builder_assignments does, with a version naming it. With since_version, the version an earlier call returned, the call waits until the list differs from it, for example because Highbay accepted the tests, the user built the change again or dropped the build, or a verification of the build passed, and otherwise returns the unchanged list after a bounded wait of about 30 seconds. Without since_version it returns at once. It records nothing and moves no working copy. A builder uses it in place of repeated list calls while it waits, whether or not Chorus delivers reminders. Each call is traced but never saved in the diagnostics history list_traces reads, so a waiting builder does not push real operations out of view.

get.description: Return the test writer's assignment list, as list_test_writer_assignments does, with a version naming it. With since_version, the version an earlier call returned, the call waits until the list differs from it, for example because Highbay's check of a report reached a verdict, the user built the change again or dropped the build, and otherwise returns the unchanged list after a bounded wait of about 30 seconds. The list holds the assignment only while the role has work: a check that accepts the tests removes it, as a drop does, so an empty list alone does not say which happened; get_test_writer_assignment does. Without since_version it returns at once. It records nothing and moves no working copy. A test writer uses it in place of repeated list calls while it waits, whether or not Chorus delivers reminders. Each call is traced but never saved in the diagnostics history list_traces reads, so a waiting test writer does not push real operations out of view.

get.description: Return the builder's assignment for the open build's change in full and record that the builder read it at its revision. The first read of a new build joins the builder's working copy to the build's own branch, highbay/build-<n> at the build's base: a copy with uncommitted work on an earlier build branch first gets that work committed there with the message "Left uncommitted when change <change_id> started"; a copy with nothing uncommitted joins from any branch. A copy with uncommitted work on any other branch, or a Git operation in progress, is refused with copy_off_branch, and a copy whose turn is held with working_copy_busy; nothing is marked read then. Building the change again makes the assignment unread.

409.description:
no_build: The user dropped this change's build: stop work on it and make no more edits or commits for it. The user starts builds on the views page.

copy_off_branch: Your working copy cannot join the build: it holds uncommitted work on a branch that is not an earlier build branch, or a Git operation is in progress. The message states the facts and the goal; put your work right with git, then read the assignment again.

working_copy_busy: Highbay is starting a build in your working folder, or files there changed while Highbay moved it (nothing was lost); call get_builder_assignment again.

working_folder_missing: Your working folder is missing; ask the user to build this change again on the views page.

get.description: Return the test writer's assignment for a change in full (the working folder, the design and Story as agreed at the built revision, the user's confirmed answers, confirmation examples and preserved behaviors of that revision, the tests it requires, and the state with the text of any findings) and record that the test writer read it at its revision. Later revisions do not change what the build saved. A new build of the change replaces the assignment, which then counts as unread, and so does each verdict of Highbay's check. The first read of a new build joins your working copy to the build's branch, highbay/tests-<n> at the build's base. A read that marks the assignment read also writes the required tests' generated folder into your copy. A copy with uncommitted work on an earlier tests build branch first gets that work committed there; a clean copy joins from any branch. Other uncommitted work or a Git operation is refused with copy_off_branch; nothing is marked read then.

Every report raises the build's report number by one and makes the state reported, from any state, clearing an earlier verdict, and returns at once. Highbay then checks the tests in the working folder against the build's Story; its verdict, needs_changes, accepted or could_not_run, replaces reported in the test writer's assignment, which then counts as unread. get.description: Return the current change list's version as soon as it differs from since, the version of the list the caller last read, or after a bounded wait of a few seconds when nothing changed. The version also changes when a card's get_build view changes (including the builder's branch head_commit or latest check), the owner's Story evaluation starts, finishes or is replaced, or a public fact in get_team or get_live_target changes. The views page keeps one such read open and, only when the version changed, calls list_changes again and, while it shows the Story, get_story_refresh. post.description: Record Checkpoint 5 approval for the owner's confirmed Change Card revision. The control plane chooses the tests' commit the same way verify_change does (the suite commit in the project's stored verification settings, or the tests Highbay accepted for the change's build at request_revision), loads the verification report by digest, re-derives the report from its evidence with verify.Approve, and records the approval on the card when the report passed for candidate_commit, request_revision, and that tests' commit. When promotion settings are configured with highbay promotion set (or a PromotionTarget is bound), approve_merge also checks that the staged binaries in <release_dir>/<candidate_commit>/ match the report's binary digests and records those digests in artifacts; without promotion settings, no release folder or staged binaries are required and artifacts is empty. The report's suite_id and environment are what the tests at suite_commit declared and are recorded on the approval without a separate comparison. Nothing is merged or deployed. It checks again, with git, that the candidate is on the build's branch, descends from its base and holds no other build's work.

404.description: not_found: No Change Card exists with this change_id.

409.description:
build_branch_mismatch: The run's candidate is no longer on the build's branch, or that branch now holds another build's work: the builder verifies again, then the user approves that run.

conflict: The Change Card is not confirmed, its request_revision does not match, or the accepted tests changed while approving; confirm the card, read the current revision with get_change, or approve again.

no_build: Without stored verification settings: the user has not built the change's revision in force with a test writer, so no tests are accepted for it. The message names the revision built, if any, and ends with the user's step.

tests_not_accepted: Without stored verification settings: Highbay has not accepted the tests of the change's build. The message names the test writer's state and who acts, and ends with the step.

422.description: unprocessable: The verification report did not pass or does not match the Change Card, the chosen tests' commit, or (when promotion settings are configured) the promotion target's staged binary digests.

501.description: not_implemented: This control plane has no verification configuration bound to it.

post.description: Confirm or refine a Checkpoint 1 Change Card with the complete ambiguity answers and example table, or adopt the revision the guide proposed beside a confirmed card. Only the user's browser session calls it, from the views page; the guide revises with revise_change and never confirms. Naming the proposed revision's request_revision adopts it: its questions are answered, it becomes the confirmed revision in force under a new request_revision with no approval, and the proposal is gone. While a proposal waits, refining the confirmed revision is refused: adopt or decline the proposal first. Otherwise the request names the card's request_revision: changed answers or examples produce a new request_revision; unchanged ones return the card as it is, with a saved approval returned in approval only while its suite_commit is still the tests' commit chosen for this revision and either no promotion target is configured or its binary digests still match the promotion target's current binaries, or in unverified_approval when a promotion target is configured and cannot measure the candidate's binaries. A decision that no option expresses goes to the guide, which records it with revise_change; the user then confirms the resulting revision. The same holds for an option the draft does not implement: when a question names its draft_option, any other answer is refused until the guide has revised the change so the design, Story, examples and preserved behaviors implement it.

post.description: Return the Checkpoint 2 C4 container topology, tool contracts, and Goa-AI guardrails of a confirmed Change Card's agreed revision, from the architecture its refresh evaluated and the revision saved; it reads and evaluates no file. It refuses a design with no Goa API or Service container and an agent without positive TimeBudget and DefaultCaps(MaxToolCalls). The result reports what the design declares; it does not compare the design with the Change Card's requirements. The guide sees the architecture of an unsaved draft with highbay preview -dir <draft_folder>.

post.description: Save a new Checkpoint 1 Change Card from a feature request and the caller's analysis of it. Highbay checks the analysis's structure and cross-field rules, gives ambiguities the IDs <change_id>-ambiguity-NN and examples the IDs check_01, check_02, ... in list order, binds the card to the authenticated owner, and computes request_revision. With story_refresh_op_id, Highbay saves what that succeeded refresh_story operation evaluated: the draft's design, Stories, architecture, go.mod and made-from list; it reads no file. A project with a go.mod requires story_refresh_op_id for a new card; with neither a go.mod nor an op_id, the card records no design. An op_id whose refresh read the draft before the user dropped a build is refused with drafted_before_drop. Every card waits for user confirmation, including a card without ambiguities. Highbay runs no model for this step and cannot judge whether the analysis is complete or correct.

drafted_before_drop: A build was dropped after this refresh. Call refresh_story to remake and evaluate the draft.

conflict: A Change Card with this change_id already exists; use revise_change or a new change_id.

422.description: unprocessable: The request could not be accepted: change_id or prompt is blank, an ambiguity repeats an option, story_refresh_op_id does not name the owner's current succeeded refresh_story operation, or the project folder holds a go.mod and story_refresh_op_id is missing. The message says which; nothing was saved.

post.description: Save the next revision of an existing Checkpoint 1 Change Card from the change's complete feature request as it now stands, a note saying what this revision changes and why, and the guide's analysis. Only the guide revises a change; only the user confirms or adopts a revision, with confirm_intent on the views page. The request is bound to the latest revision: the proposed revision's request_revision when one waits, otherwise the card's. On a card that was never confirmed, the new revision replaces it. On a confirmed card, the new revision is saved as the proposed revision beside the confirmed one, replacing any earlier proposal, and the confirmed revision stays in force with its answers, confirmation, approval, Stories and design source until the user adopts the proposal with confirm_intent or declines it. The analysis accounts for every example of the revision it revises exactly once, keeping or editing it through prior_id or dropping it through removed_example_ids. Highbay keeps the IDs of kept examples, gives new examples the lowest check_NN ID neither card uses, adopts the evaluated draft's design, Stories, architecture, go.mod and made-from list when story_refresh_op_id is given, without reading any file, or keeps every snapshot field of the revision it revises when it is omitted, even with zero Stories, and saves the new revision in needs_confirmation status for the user's review. The new revision has no answers, confirmed_by or approval: earlier decisions carry over only where the analysis restates them in its summary, examples or preserved behaviors. The result is the change as get_change returns it. Highbay runs no model for this step and cannot judge whether the analysis is complete or correct. A project with a go.mod refuses an omitted op_id when the revision being revised has no design. A refresh from before the user dropped a build is refused with drafted_before_drop.

A recorded approval is returned in approval only while its suite_commit is still the tests' commit chosen for this revision and either no promotion target is configured or its binary digests still match the promotion target's current binaries, or in unverified_approval when a promotion target is configured and cannot measure the candidate's binaries.

get.description: Return a change's build when it is the project's open build, with whether the user has taken it: building, passed with the commits to merge, merged, or dropped. not_started when it is not, including a builder-only build whose stored verification settings were removed; start a new build on the views page. Otherwise return the revision built, when, whether each role read its assignment, the builder's branch, while the build is still building its head_commit once the branch advances past the build's base, and its latest completed check_project verdict, the test writer's state with the number of Highbay's findings (never their text), and whether the build is for the change's revision in force. post.description: The user starts building a confirmed change at its agreed revision, the one in force, on the project owner's bound team. A project has one open build. Building another change is refused with previous_change_open until the user has merged a passed run of the open build into the branch checked out in the project folder or dropped it with drop_build. Building the open build's own change again keeps its number and base and replaces its assignments; while no verification of it has passed, replaces must name the open build the page showed, else unfinished_build_open; once that build is merged or dropped, building its change again starts a new build. Highbay first checks, without effects, merge or drop, a revision drafted before a drop, and the agreed design against the project's commit; numbers a new build one more than any highbay/build-<n> or highbay/tests-<n> branch and the open build; and saves it with its base, the project's commit, by one rename. Then it makes a missing working copy (.highbay-build, and .highbay-tests when a test writer is used) on the build's own branch and registers the builder and the test writer in their copies. Build moves no existing copy: each joins the build's branch when its worker first reads the assignment. A refused start saves nothing; after the save, a server stop leaves the build saved, and building again makes a missing copy and registers the roles. After the start's turns are released, bringing the team up has its own 45-second limit. get_build reads the saved build without this start's transient team outcome.

conflict: The Change Card is not confirmed or request_revision is not its agreed revision (a waiting proposal's revision cannot be built), or the agreed revision records no design to build from; nothing changed.

not_repository: The project folder is not in a Git repository, which every build's working copies need; nothing was saved. The message ends with the step to create or select a repository.

no_commit: The project repository has no commit for the build's working copies to start from; nothing was saved. The message ends with the step to make its first commit.

no_test_layout: This project has neither stored verification settings nor Highbay's test layout; nothing was saved. Store verification settings, then build again.

git_identity_missing: Git has no configured name and address, which Highbay uses to commit what a working copy left when it joins a new build and to record accepted tests; nothing was saved. Configure Git's name and address, then build again.

copy_folder_in_use: A working copy's folder in the project folder, .highbay-build or .highbay-tests, is a file or a folder that is not a linked working copy of the project's repository; nothing was saved. The message names the folder and ends with the step to move it out of the project.

tests_branch_in_use: The branch Highbay checks out in a missing working copy, highbay/build-<n> or highbay/tests-<n>, is checked out in another folder; nothing was saved. The message names that folder, quoted, and ends with the step that frees the branch.

working_copy_busy: Another build is starting, a worker is reading its assignment into its working copy, or a test check holds the test writer's working copy; nothing was saved. Start the build again when that has ended.

previous_change_open: Another change's build is open, and the user has neither merged a passed run of it into the branch checked out in the project folder nor dropped it; nothing was saved. The body names that build, with the commits to merge once a run passed, so the page offers the merge commands and Drop.

unfinished_build_open: Building this change again replaces its open build, which no verification has passed, and replaces does not name that build; nothing was saved. The page asks the user first, then sends replaces naming the build it showed.

drafted_before_drop: The agreed revision was drafted before the user dropped another change, so its design can hold that change's design; nothing was saved. The guide revises the change from its draft; the user adopts the revision, then builds.

design_changed_outside: A design file at the build's base commit is not a version the agreed revision was made from: it was changed outside Highbay; nothing was saved. The message names the file and the commit. When the change is uncommitted, commit the design change in the project folder first; then the guide calls update_draft, refresh_story and revise_change, and the user adopts the revision and builds.

It changes no working copy, branch, draft or file of the user's: the build's commits stay on its branches, and the guide's next refresh_story makes the draft again from the project folder. post.description: The highbay command, after it confirms the project server's identity, hands over the request settings of each model provider whose key is set in the shell it runs in: the key and the listed settings that route and authenticate the provider's requests. The project server holds them in memory only and forgets them when it stops. A live target using stored verification settings receives the chosen provider's held settings; a verification with that evaluator receives every held provider's settings. Accepted written tests receive no provider settings in verification or live targets: for a direct live model the executor serves an executor-owned loopback model gateway. It has no authentication: any local process, including another user's, can use it while the target runs without receiving the provider key. The check helper receives none. An absent provider attribute keeps what is held for that provider. A present one replaces everything held for it and must include the provider's key variable; an empty one is refused, because it is neither a way to keep nor a way to forget. A request with neither attribute changes nothing and reports what is held. When no model is chosen and a provider is now held, live targets use that provider's default model, anthropic before openai; any other choice stays. The result names the held variables and the model choice, never a value. Only the highbay command's management credential may call this operation; it is never an MCP tool.

Return bounded safe summaries newest first, without reading the entire file. Older pages and later refreshes work on the same running server and after restart. Recording is automatic in the project server. Authenticated HTTP/MCP domain calls have a highbay.request.<operation> boundary span, with child domain operations recorded separately. Reads by the user's views page that succeed or are refused (sent with GET, such as the reads the page repeats whenever the project changes) are exported but not added to this private history; such a read that ends with an error status or a panic is added. Waiting reads are never added, whoever sends them; every other agent call and every operation that changes something is added. Requests rejected before authentication or decoding and separate verification processes are absent.

post.description: The guide brings design changes made outside Highbay into its draft, before drafting a new change and when told a design file changed in the project folder. Under the draft's lock Highbay compares each design file's draft and live versions over a recorded base. The history base is the latest recorded version present in the project's committed history since the draft's start, or the starting folder version when that history supplies none. The comparison base is whichever of that history base and the outside version the draft last took was recorded later; with no previous take, it is the history base. A live version equal to the comparison base brings nothing. If the project's committed history gained a recorded version since the last take, Highbay takes and reports the live version without merging it. Otherwise an outside change is taken when the draft did not change that file, merged with git merge-file when both changed it, and listed to correct when both changed the same lines or one side removed what the other changed. A draft file Go cannot parse, and a module the project's go.mod requires at another version or with another replace directive than the draft's, are listed to correct; Highbay does not merge go.mod. Each listed file names the folder that holds it: the guide corrects a file of its draft, while a design file or go.mod of the project folder that cannot be parsed is the user's to correct there and the guide never edits it. When the project's commit, the draft, the project's files or the draft's made-from list change while Highbay prepares the update, Highbay brings nothing and answers conflict, and the guide calls update_draft again. Highbay records an interrupted update so a later call can finish it without merging its result again; if the guide changed the file in between, the file is listed to correct. An uncommitted revert to an older version may bring nothing; when a build reports design_changed_outside for an uncommitted design change, the user commits the change in the project folder, then asks the guide to call update_draft, refresh_story and revise_change. Otherwise call refresh_story after this update. Takes no input.

post.description: Write the open build's agreed design into the builder's working folder and regenerate its code. Highbay replaces, creates or removes the Go files under the builder's design/ so that design/ holds exactly the build's design source (never a test file or testdata; a linked design/ is refused), then compares each module the design imports with the go.mod the revision was made from: when the builder's go.mod lacks a module or requires an older version, the call names go get <module>@<version> and go mod tidy, prefixed GOWORK=off when the assignment's gowork_off is true, writes design/ and generates nothing until they are run. A differing replace directive for a module the design imports is also named, including the saved replacement line or the fact that none was saved, so the builder corrects go.mod before calling again. Otherwise it compiles and runs the design as an ordinary process with the user's file and network access and atomically replaces gen/, preserving top-level user files and leaving go.mod and go.sum unchanged. With target eval it regenerates the working folder's eval/ module from its own design. Return the written paths and warnings; a warning after gen/ publication still means generation succeeded. It compiles the design only; it does not build the application or run tests.

post.description: Read the guide's draft, .highbay-draft in the project folder: its go.mod, go.sum and the Go files under design/ in gofmt form, never the rest of the project. When the draft is missing, Highbay makes it first, from the newest design a Change Card holds whose versions are all on the draft's made-from list, with the project's go.mod and go.sum, or else from the project folder; after the user dropped a build, it makes the draft again from the project folder and says so in message until a revision is saved. Compute the canonical snapshot_digest and start or reuse the project owner's in-memory Story refresh operation, which every caller acting for the owner reads; it is reused only while the draft and its made-from list are unchanged. Return promptly with op_id, state, snapshot_digest and draft_folder while evaluation continues on a server-owned context that survives client disconnects. A succeeded operation keeps the design, Stories, architecture, the draft's go.mod and the made-from list it read; propose_change and revise_change save them with the revision. A design file Go cannot parse, or one that imports a package of the project outside design/, is refused with its file and line.

ApprovalItem.description: Checkpoint 5 approval recorded by approve_merge after the verification report passed and matched the change being promoted: the exact candidate commit, the tests' commit chosen for the revision, and (when promotion settings are configured) the binary digests the promotion target measured. suite_id and environment record what the tests at suite_commit declared in the report and are shown, not compared against separate promotion settings. test_source is derived on each read from how the server chooses tests. The approval is saved with the card in the control plane's cards directory, merges and deploys nothing, is replaced by the next successful approve_merge for the same revision, and is dropped when the user refines the confirmed revision or adopts a proposed one with confirm_intent. A revise_change on a confirmed card leaves it on the confirmed revision, which stays in force until the user adopts the proposal. get_change and confirm_intent return it in approval while the tests' commit chosen for the revision still equals suite_commit and (when a promotion target is configured) the promotion target's current binary digests still equal artifacts, or in unverified_approval when the tests' commit still matches but a configured promotion target cannot verify the candidate's binaries on that read.

ambiguities.description: Open questions only the requester can answer: product, domain, or operational choices that change user-visible behavior. Never ask whether to replace Highbay's worked example or ask about internal Go/Goa plumbing. Do not ask about details the request already settles; state settled product defaults in summary, or in examples when they change an observable outcome. Send an empty list when nothing is open.

examples.description: Concrete acceptance examples in plain domain terms, never placeholder text or leftovers of Highbay's worked example; each becomes a check the change must pass.

preserved_behaviors.description: Existing user-facing behaviors of an established product that this change must keep, each stated in plain domain terms; send an empty list ([]) on a new product (including the first change after init_project: a blank project has no behavior to keep, and Highbay's worked example is replaced rather than preserved) or when none apply.

summary.description: Concise plain-English description (2–4 sentences) of what the product or change will do for its users and the key product defaults your draft settles. Never describe file paths, candidate runner flags, or removal of Highbay's worked example.

Refer to an ambiguity or example only by its 1-based position in this analysis (1 is the first); never invent identifiers. Highbay saves it unchanged without checking it; the views page validates and renders it. Omit it when a plain card is clearer.

CP1Analysis.description: Product-level Change Card shown to the requester on the Highbay browser page to confirm intent before code is written. Write every field for a requester who knows only their own goal, not the repository: use plain domain language about observable user behavior, never repository file paths (such as design/design.go), Highbay candidate runner flags (such as -listen), or internal Goa/Goa-AI symbol names unless the requester explicitly asked about a CLI or API surface. When the project was created with Highbay's worked example (init_project with worked_example: true) and the requester is building their own product, replace that example silently in your draft: never mention or ask about it on the Change Card. Highbay checks structure and cross-field rules; it cannot judge whether the analysis is complete or correct.

draft_option.description: The one string in options, character for character, that the draft design, Story, examples and preserved behaviors you send with this proposal already implement. Set it whenever choosing another option would require changing any of them. The user can then confirm only this option on the page; when they want another, the page sends them back to you, and you revise the change (revise_change) so the draft implements their choice before they confirm. Omit it only when every option works with the draft exactly as it stands.

options.description: At least two distinct, self-contained choices; each states the behavior it selects and what follows from it. The requester's answer must be exactly one of these strings.

question.description: The decision in plain language, saying what the choice changes.

CP1AnalysisAmbiguity.description: One product, domain, or operational choice only the requester can make. Highbay gives it the ID <change_id>-ambiguity-NN, numbered in list order.

expected_outcome.description: The observable result or refusal that must hold.

input_summary.description: The actual request, inputs, and starting state in this scenario, with real values from the request and the design, never placeholders.

scenario.description: Short name of the situation, in the requester's domain terms.

verification_kind.description: deterministic when code can check the outcome directly; model_judged when checking it needs judgment.

CP1AnalysisExample.description: One concrete acceptance example that becomes a check the change must pass. Highbay gives it the ID check_01, check_02, ... in list order.

ambiguities.description: Open questions only the requester can answer: product, domain, or operational choices that change user-visible behavior. Never ask about Highbay's worked example or internal Go/Goa plumbing. Do not ask about details the request, the design or a confirmed answer already settle; state settled product defaults in summary, or in examples when they change an observable outcome. Send an empty list when nothing is open.

examples.description: Concrete acceptance examples in plain domain terms. Give prior_id for each current example you keep or edit; omit it for new ones.

preserved_behaviors.description: Existing user-facing behaviors of the product that this revision must keep, each stated in plain domain terms; empty when none apply.

removed_example_ids.description: IDs of the current card's examples this revision drops. Every current example ID appears exactly once, either as an examples[].prior_id or here; send an empty list when none are dropped.

summary.description: Concise plain-English description (2–4 sentences) of the revised product behavior and settled product defaults, without file paths, candidate runner flags, or references to Highbay's worked example.

ui_composition.description: Optional OpenUI Lang program that helps the requester decide the open questions, built only from the decision components the highbay://golden-path resource lists. Refer to an ambiguity or example only by its 1-based position in this analysis (1 is the first); never invent identifiers. Highbay saves it unchanged without checking it; the views page validates and renders it. Omit it when a plain card is clearer.

CP1RevisionAnalysis.description: Updated product-level Change Card shown to the requester on the Highbay browser page, analyzed against the current Change Card (as get_change returns it at request_revision), the draft design, and highbay://golden-path. Write every field for a requester who knows their own goal, not the repository: use plain domain language without file paths (such as design/design.go), Highbay candidate runner flags (such as -listen), references to Highbay's worked example, or internal Goa/Goa-AI symbol names unless the requester explicitly asked about a CLI or API surface. A confirmed answer stays settled unless the revised request or design contradicts it: do not ask it again, and restate it in summary, examples or preserved_behaviors, because the revised card drops every answer. An explicit instruction in the revised request or design replaces the decisions, examples and preserved behaviors it affects. An unanswered question stays in ambiguities unless the revised request or design answers it or removes its scope. Everything else on the current card stays unless the revised request or design changes it. Highbay checks the structure and the example accounting; it cannot judge whether the analysis is complete or correct.

expected_outcome.description: The observable result or refusal that must hold.

input_summary.description: The actual request, inputs, and starting state in this scenario, with real values from the request and the design, never placeholders.

prior_id.description: ID of the current card's example this one keeps or edits, exactly as the card shows it; the example keeps that ID. Omit it for a new example, which gets the lowest check_NN ID the current and revised cards do not use.

scenario.description: Short name of the situation, in the requester's domain terms.

verification_kind.description: deterministic when code can check the outcome directly; model_judged when checking it needs judgment.

CP1RevisionAnalysisExample.description: One concrete acceptance example of the revised card: a current example kept or edited in place (prior_id set), or a new one.

chorus_status.description: Whether Chorus responded to the latest conversation read.

messages.description: Chronological messages across the project's #channel and @you direct messages.

TeamConversation.description: Ordered messages and pinned collaboration manifest for the project's Chorus team.

id.description: Unique message key combining target and sequence (for example #ops-8f3a1c902b4e:12).

model.description: Reported model or participant kind (for example human, service, or model name).

reply_to.description: Optional sequence number in target that this message replies to.

sender_role.description: Project role of the sender for UI presentation.

sent_at_ms.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when Chorus recorded the message.

target.description: Chorus target (#channel or @handle) carrying this message.

TeamMessage.description: One message in the project's Chorus channel or direct-message thread.

assignment.description: unread when this worker owes an assignment read; nothing_owed when it has work and owes no read; no_work when the open build needs nothing from it; unknown when assignments could not be read. The guide has no assignments (no_work).

attention.description: Reported block kind when the role needs the user (for example permission, question, auth, or silent after 60 seconds without progress).

has_terminal.description: True when this role has a managed or attached herdr-core terminal that can be opened in the browser terminal drawer.

state.description: Current role state; unknown means herdr-core and Chorus cannot establish it.

TeamRoleState.description: Observed terminal, Chorus liveness, attention, and assignment state of one registered project role.

chorus_status.description: Whether Highbay's local Chorus connection is healthy.

roles.description: Registered roles in guide, builder, test_writer order; empty before registration.

team.description: Stable Chorus swarm name for this project.

TeamSnapshot.description: Current project team roles, saved CLI choices, dismissed notices, and Chorus connectivity.

example.team: Sed libero qui vel et aut in.

cause.description: What could not be used: stopping (the server is shutting down), chorus (the local Chorus server is unavailable), hc (herdr-core is unavailable or a terminal command failed), project_state (the project's private record or an agent credential could not be read or written), or role_folder (a role's working folder could not be prepared).

TeamUnavailable.description: Structured failure cause returned when project team preparation or agent launch cannot proceed.

focused.description: Whether the terminal drawer currently holds focus.

bytes.description: Number of output bytes consumed by xterm.js.

TerminalClientFrame.description: Client-to-server WebSocket message carrying user keystrokes, viewport resize, focus state, or flow-control credit.

exit_code.description: Process exit status when the terminal process exited normally.

reason.description: Stream end reason reported by herdr-core (for example detached, exited, killed, or lost).
reason.example: Blanditiis voluptate rem tempora est est.

signal.description: Terminating signal number when the terminal process was ended by a signal.

example.reason: Blanditiis voluptate rem tempora est est.

TerminalServerFrame.description: Server-to-client WebSocket message carrying raw PTY output bytes, external grid resizes, or stream termination.

expires_at.description: UTC expiration timestamp of the ticket.

ticket.description: Opaque single-use ticket valid for at most 30 seconds.

TerminalTicketResult.description: Single-use short-lived ticket passed on the attach_role_terminal WebSocket upgrade query.

working_folder.description: Folder to write the tests in: your own working copy of the project, .highbay-tests, on the build's branch highbay/tests-<n>. Do not commit there: Highbay commits what it accepts.

TestWriterAssignment.description: The test writer's assignment for one build: write the required tests for the Story as agreed at the built revision, in the test module (eval/) of the working folder, and make them hold the service to the user's confirmed answers, confirmation examples and preserved behaviors of that revision, which the assignment carries exactly as confirmed. Highbay writes eval/design/story_tests.go, which declares the required tests, from the agreed Story and generates the module at each read that marks the assignment read and again at each report; the test writer leaves that file as it is. After changing the module's design, the test writer reports to have it generated again or runs highbay gen -dir eval in the working folder first; regenerating keeps the required tests. go build ./... in eval/ checks the work before a report, and Highbay's check of each report is the judge.

tags.name: project
tags.description: Owns one local project's server identity, agent credentials, self-update lifecycle, and origin-scoped browser session. Management credentials last for one listening server and never authorize application decisions; besides this service, they may only hand over the model provider request settings of the shell running highbay (the highbay service's hand_over_model_settings). This service is not exposed as agent tools.

tags.name: highbay
tags.description: Owns Highbay's software factory lifecycle across Checkpoint 1 intent and Story Change Cards, Checkpoint 2 C4 architecture and guardrail previews, Checkpoint 3 live target prompt overrides, Checkpoint 4 verification runs, Checkpoint 5 promotion approvals and merges, and the browser workspace's team conversation and terminal controls.
